chunks: He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Nahwi, the companion of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari, reported to me from Abu Bakr, from al-Abbas ibn al-Husayn al-Lahabi, from Ibn Hassan, from Qubaysah al-Lahabi, who said:

Ali ibn Hafs ibn Umar wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur that he found in an inn at Multan the writing of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them): "When I reached this place, and my blood had turned, I said: Perhaps a drinking-fountain will clear and quench the thirst * that the muddied watering-hole prolonged. Perhaps the bare sides will be clothed * and the humiliated, the wronged one, will be aided. Perhaps the Mender of the broken bone, by His grace * will find ease and mend it. Perhaps Allah -- let the servant not despair, for indeed He * eases what is great and immense."

The Shaykh said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar recited to me by Abu Bakr al-Urzumi: "I see a weak man called bold for his oppression * but if charged with piety, his tools would fail. And a chaste man called weak for his chastity * but were it not for piety, his paths would not fail him. And a fool favored in his affairs * his brothers and relatives lord over him. Without wisdom in affairs nor piety * nor an excellent one whose gifts are counted. But it is the grip and expansion of God * so neither can this fight Him nor that overcome Him. When the Merciful perfects a person's intellect * then indeed his morals and purposes are perfected."

key_terms.المنصور: Al-Mansur -- the Abbasid Caliph Abu Ja'far
key_terms.المولتان: Multan -- a city in modern Pakistan, refuge of Alid fugitives
key_terms.جابر العظم الكسير: The Mender of the broken bone -- epithet for God

ai.seo_question: What is the poem written by Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan at Multan?
ai.summary: This narration preserves two remarkable literary pieces: first, a poem inscribed by Abdullah ibn Muhammad, a descendant of Imam Ali, at an inn in Multan (modern Pakistan) while fleeing Abbasid persecution under Caliph al-Mansur. The verses express hope in God's mercy during exile and hardship. Second, a poem by al-Urzumi reflecting on the irony that the pious appear weak while oppressors appear strong, concluding that all is in God's hands and true perfection lies in intellect and morals.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 10. He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Nahwi, the friend of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Ambari, reported to me from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibnal-Qasim, who reported from al-Abbas ibn al-Husayn al-Lahabi, who reported from al-Hassan, from Qubaisah al-Lahabi, who said:

‘Ali ibn Hafs ibn Umar wrote to Abu Ja’far al-Mansoor that I saw it written in a khan at Multan that: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali Abi Talib (peace be upon him) says: When I reached this place, and found myself secure, I said: "Perchance, the drinking fountain may clear up to quench the thirst, a thirst which has been prolonged because of the turbid water, Perchance, you may be garbed by the unclothed one, and may find help from the lowly and oppressed; Perchance a bonesetter of the broken bone may from his kindness, feel sympathy for the broken bone and set it. Perchance, Allah may not allow His slave to despair, for all that is lofty and great is indeed negligible in His sight."

Sheikh said: And Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar recited to me quoting Abu Bakr al-Arzami, the following:- "(In this world) I find a (feeble) helpless person known as tough because of his tyranny, (but) had he adopted fear of Allah, his brutality might have been blunted; And (I find) a chaste person taken as helpless, because of his (virtue of) chastity (and modesty) (though) had it not been for fear of Allah, the ways (of evil) would not have found him powerless; And (I find) a fool whose affairs are cared for (by others), being appointed a leader by his fellowmen and his relatives, (in spite of the fact that) he has no resoluteness in his affairs, nor are nobility and magnanimity counted among his qualities. But all that is controlled by Allah, and He grants, So neither this contends him nor that tries to overcome him; (The truth is that) when Allah in His mercy, perfects the wisdom of a person, his behaviour and all his desires are perfected also."
